purpose: Constrain an AI tabletop role-play with peer-reviewed behavioral mechanisms and turn those mechanisms into observable human-study risks. No source proves product performance or replaces participant evidence.

evidencePolicy.minimum: Every simulation behavior assumption must cite at least one peer-reviewed source below.
evidencePolicy.interpretation: Sources support mechanisms and study design only. Product-specific outcomes remain unverified assumptions until recorded in the signed independent study.
evidencePolicy.alcoholSafety: Model alcohol as a variable cognitive-load condition only. Do not encourage drinking, administer alcohol, or infer impairment from identity or appearance.

peerReviewedSources.citation: McPhee, M. D., & Hendershot, C. S. (2023). Meta-analysis of acute alcohol effects on response inhibition. Neuroscience & Biobehavioral Reviews, 152, 105274.
peerReviewedSources.supports: Acute alcohol exposure has a pooled detrimental effect on response inhibition in laboratory Go/No-Go and Stop-Signal studies; effect magnitude and moderators vary.

peerReviewedSources.citation: Steele, C. M., & Josephs, R. A. (1990). Alcohol myopia: Its prized and dangerous effects. American Psychologist, 45(8), 921–933.
peerReviewedSources.supports: Alcohol-myopia theory frames acute alcohol effects as narrowed attention to salient cues; it does not license a deterministic prediction about any individual.

peerReviewedSources.citation: Bond, R., & Smith, P. B. (1996). Culture and conformity: A meta-analysis of studies using Asch's line judgment task. Psychological Bulletin, 119(1), 111–137.
peerReviewedSources.supports: Conformity effects have been studied across many Asch-type experiments and vary by context and culture; a loud first answer is a study risk, not an assumed group outcome.

peerReviewedSources.citation: Sowden, S., et al. (2018). Quantifying compliance and acceptance through public and private social conformity. Consciousness and Cognition, 65, 359–367.
peerReviewedSources.supports: Public compliance and private acceptance are distinct social-influence phenomena, motivating a comparison between a shared group commit and a private relay commit.

peerReviewedSources.citation: Peelle, J. E. (2018). Listening effort: How the cognitive consequences of acoustic challenge are reflected in brain and behavior. Ear and Hearing, 39(2), 204–214.
peerReviewedSources.supports: Acoustically degraded speech can impose cognitive demand and interfere with other operations; it motivates high-noise readability and comprehension tests, not a universal failure prediction.

peerReviewedSources.citation: Granovskiy, B., Gold, J. M., Sumpter, D. J. T., & Goldstone, R. L. (2015). Integration of Social Information by Human Groups. Topics in Cognitive Science, 7(3), 469–493.
peerReviewedSources.supports: Social information can shift individual judgments, with heterogeneous susceptibility; this supports observing dissent and turn-taking rather than declaring consensus inherently good or bad.

gates.risk: A salient quote, attribution, timer, or loud group reaction can eclipse game context or completed truth meaning.
gates.simulationPrompt: Can every role state the game context before reveal and the complete truth status after reveal when attention is deliberately divided?
gates.humanStudyEvidence: Individual explanation of authentic, fabricated-for-game, disputed, source-unavailable, and removed states; screenshot, recording, photograph, and reasonable-crop inspection.
gates.failClosedRule: Any real participant truth or game-context misunderstanding remains a stop signal under the signed plan.

gates.risk: Fast movement, a prepotent response, or fragmented attention can produce accidental or duplicate answers.
gates.simulationPrompt: Does each candidate make readiness, the current control, and recovery visible without exposing the forehead card or changing score semantics?
gates.humanStudyEvidence: Accidental commits, duplicate commits, fallback use, and unrecovered selected-path failures by condition and access path.
gates.failClosedRule: Two unrecovered selected-direction path failures remain a stop signal under the signed plan.

gates.risk: A loud or early speaker can suppress disagreement, especially when the holder is blind and must act on group guidance.
gates.simulationPrompt: Can a quiet dissenting role contribute before a shared commit, and does the private countermodel change the pressure pattern rather than merely hide it?
gates.humanStudyEvidence: Facilitator observation of who speaks before commit, whether disagreement is acknowledged, and whether participants can explain who is entitled to commit.
gates.failClosedRule: Do not treat speed, shouting, peer pressure, or alcohol as product success metrics.

gates.risk: Noise and divided attention can make a statement seem readable while degrading comprehension, role memory, and next-action recall.
gates.simulationPrompt: Do maximum-length text, attribution, role instruction, recovery copy, and truth labels remain understandable when social audio competes for attention?
gates.humanStudyEvidence: Correct first-read, role recall, state explanation, and recovery completion at frozen distance, angle, light, and noise conditions.
gates.failClosedRule: Never use subjective confidence alone as proof of comprehension.

gates.risk: Fast social transitions can leak the forehead card, prior result, or turn ownership; a nominal tap or screen-reader alternative can become socially second-class.
gates.simulationPrompt: Can every role complete the same score, review, report, and rematch semantics through tap-only, no-motion, VoiceOver, and TalkBack paths without protected-information leakage?
gates.humanStudyEvidence: Role-specific task completion and privacy checks with participants who regularly use the relevant access paths.
gates.failClosedRule: Any accessibility route that leaks the active forehead card or cannot complete the role-appropriate round blocks approval.

gates.risk: A confusing misfire can turn into blame, social pressure, or a perceived unfair score rather than a recoverable moment.
gates.simulationPrompt: Does recovery use plain, neutral language, preserve round context, and avoid an unsafe undo that changes the truth or score record?
gates.humanStudyEvidence: Observed recovery after sensor, interruption, orientation, offline report, and protected-handoff states; participant explanation of the next safe action.
gates.failClosedRule: A recovery path may not silently reinterpret a tilt, expose a protected card, or claim a queued report was adjudicated.
